evidence: Cic. Fam. 16.24.2: ego vix teneor quīn accurram (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 2.28: ex hominum mīlibus LX vix ad D sēsē redāctōs esse dīxērunt (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The everyday word: “with difficulty, only just”. With numbers, “barely”: vix ad D, barely five hundred (Caesar). vix tandem is “at long last” (Catull. 62.2); “hardly any”, vix ūllus (Quint. 1 pr. 12, Lewis & Short); for “hardly ever” see ever.

evidence: Plaut. As. 3.2.36: aegrē nimis rīsum continuī (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 16.11: aegrē mē tenuī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: “With effort, only just”, where English says “hardly”: aegrē mē tenuī, I could hardly restrain myself. It also means “reluctantly, with displeasure”: aegrē ferre, to take something badly (Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: I can hardly keep myself from running to you

phrases.latin: sed jam vix illum adsequor currentem et intrā paucissimōs diēs nōn poterō
phrases.english: but now I can hardly catch him when he runs, and in a few days I won’t be able to

phrases.latin: ita torpentēs gelū in castra rediēre ut vix laetitiam victōriae sentīrent
phrases.english: they came back to camp so numb with cold that they could hardly feel the joy of victory
I could only just keep from laughing
